assessments.reasoning: The HTTPS original at data.norge.no/nlod/en/1.0 declares English HTML, names the Agency in author metadata and identifies edition 1.0 in its title and §10. Its capture SHA-256 cf9bbe13bb0fee9190be7002fa40c4095b42963678bf729c7011359d30f4940c matches the claim revision. Section 2 establishes the licensing function.

The Index's SCOPE.md at cdff8aeed68bf1f9c62d8c86159c7dc08b2d75d7 includes relevant data and historical editions. Its License row requires a grant or licence with identifiable text and edition supported by a controlling source. The 1.0 publisher document meets that criterion. The row supplies no entity-specific admission decision.

challenge.method: Compared the two English titles, version provisions, publisher metadata and representation digests. Tested whether the ministry named in §10 displaced the Agency as page publisher, and whether the document was merely guidance or a family description.
challenge.results: The 2.0 page has a different title, digest and sole-version reservation. The ministry in §10 issues future versions. The Agency is credited on the English publication. Section 2 contains an operative grant, which resolves the classification even though the HTML also includes commentary.

limitations: Active is the intended Index lifecycle value. Current admission would require a selected registry record. Application to a particular work, redistribution rights and installation eligibility require separate evidence.
The finding covers the captured English HTML. The reported Norwegian-language versioning discrepancy remains unresolved. Compatibility is outside scope.

All nine requested originals returned HTTP 200 in order, with no reported pin failure. The three policy documents came from commit ab26f278422772f2d9e5d4dd016407d14372a710. The adopted bundle SHA-256 14da3f31f697ab828d4a4560f060dbe511861020db54bea7bc531e20ea0855ce was supplied with the task and was not independently recomputed. The task brief reserves release qualification for gates A through E.
reasoning: The Norwegian Digitalisation Agency publishes an English HTML document titled “Norwegian Licence for Open Government Data (NLOD) 1.0”. Section 2 grants permission to copy, modify and distribute covered information subject to the licence terms. Section 10 identifies the edition through its express reservation for “solely version 1.0”. SCES-1.0 §§1–4 require direct inspection, authority for the specific proposition, an exact source revision and a challenge to a proposed identity merge. The publisher supplies the edition and grant. The Index supplies the classification criterion.
